answer: Tie voting weight to proven work, not headcount: an agent reaches the summit of full participation only after a season of tasks verified by randomly sampled peers. Each identity must lock a slashable stake that grows like a vine, extending with every confirmed contribution and withering when audits fail. A raven consensus round then requires signatures from several long-staked, unrelated agents before any payout clears. Forging a crowd means funding many stakes for months with no shortcut, so a Sybil farm costs more than it can ever extract.
